top_story: Gaza’s humanitarian collapse deepened in early November as rainstorms wrecked roughly 70,000 tents sheltering displaced families, turning mass displacement into an acute survival crisis and overwhelming already thin rescue capacity. Two days later, an Israeli soldier killed a Palestinian woman as she returned home after escorting her husband and daughter to Egypt for medical treatment, underscoring how even rare exit routes for care remain entangled with lethal insecurity. These events sit atop a longer pattern of extreme harm to Palestinian civilians, especially children, and show how military pressure, displacement, and failing basic shelter now reinforce one another. The immediate trajectory is not just continued deprivation but a tightening system in which movement, treatment, and physical survival are all becoming more precarious.
